body: This requirement primarily applies to desktop applications with auto-update features, which is outside the primary scope of ASVS. Its applicability to web applications is limited to niche cases, making it less relevant to ASVS's focus on broadly applicable security standards for web applications. Also, we have mentioned this here too: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/663#issuecomment-955805650

comments.body:
Requirement:

| # | Description | L1 | L2 | L3 | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **[10.3.1](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x18-V10-Coding.md#v103-application-integrity)** | Verify that if the application has a client or server auto-update feature, updates should be obtained over secure channels and digitally signed. The update code must validate the digital signature of the update before installing or executing the update. | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 16 |

I think web apps can still have an auto update feature making this requirement still relevant.

@elarlang @ryarmst @danielcuthbert @tobias @randomstuff, thoughts?

Debian traditionally does *not* use (by default) a secure channel but only digital signatures and (AFAIU) some timestamps in the signature in order to limit denial of update attacks. Would such a scheme be OK?

Do we need to explicitly mention that any auto-updated plugins are also covered?

> I think web apps can still have an auto update feature making this requirement still relevant.

Yes, many PHP-based apps for example have auto-updates and plugin registries.

> Do we need to explicitly mention that any auto-updated plugins are also covered?

(((Note: this might include applications which would download/update executable deep-learning models.)))

Yesterday, we had a presentation where we discussed that we shouldn't target niche applications and write requirements for them. Also, machine learning models can be downloaded or updated, but they are not essentially executable code (out of scope for ASVS).
@ryarmst what do you think about this?

As per @randomstuff it's definitely not *rare* (think CMS ecosystems). I think the `over secure channels` feels like it should be covered generally in V9, no? Otherwise, I don't have a strong opinion. Perhaps it could be captured by a separate, more general requirement, but perhaps not.

I don't think it is too niche and it is also a potentially dangerous piece of functionality. I think secure channels is worth saying explicitly although it should also cover in V9. However, I think it can be L3 and I would simplify it slightly to:

| # | Description | L1 | L2 | L3 | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **10.3.1** | [MODIFIED, LEVEL L1 > L3] Verify that, if the application has an auto-update feature, updates should be obtained over secure channels and digitally signed, with the digital signature being validated before installing or executing the update. | | | ✓ | 16 |

I would like to restate my opinion regarding secure channels with another example from V3 (section text):

> TLS or another secure transport channel is mandatory for session management. 

I feel like these are redundancies that appear littered throughout ASVS and are covered under [9.2.2](https://github.com/ryarmst/ASVS/blob/ryarmst-2102/5.0/en/0x17-V9-Communications.md#v92-general-service-to-service-communication-security).
